question.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at an arbitrary point, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+4{t}^{2}}}⟨1,2t,0⟩, \\ N(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+4{t}^{2}}}⟨-2t,1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
question.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B(t) & =T(t)\times N(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+4{t}^{2}}}⟨1,2t,0⟩\times \frac{1}{\sqrt{1+4{t}^{2}}}⟨-2t,1,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{1+4{t}^{2}}\,\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 2t & 0 \\ -2t & 1 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{1+4{t}^{2}}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}2t & 0 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 2t \\ -2t & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{1+4{t}^{2}}⟨0-0,-(0-0),1+4{t}^{2}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{1+4{t}^{2}}⟨0,0,1+4{t}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,0,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
